title: Signed Varint (ZigZag + LEB128) Encoding
description: Protocol Buffers encodes 32-bit signed integers compactly in two steps: first, **ZigZag encoding** maps signed 32-bit `n` to an unsigned 32-bit integer `u = ((n << 1) ^ (n >> 31))` (using arithmetic right shift, so `0 -> 0`, `-1 -> 1`, `1 -> 2`, `-2 -> 3`, ..., `-2^31 -> 2^32 - 1`); second, **Base-128 Varint (LEB128)** splits `u` into 7-bit groups from least significant to most significant, setting the continuation bit `0x80` (`128`) on every byte except the final byte. Given `n`, return the encoded byte sequence as an integer array with values in `[0, 255]`.
hints: Compute the unsigned 32-bit ZigZag value `u = ((n << 1) ^ (n >> 31)) & 0xFFFFFFFF` (using `Integer.toUnsignedLong` in Java so shifts stay unsigned).
While `u >= 128`, emit `(u & 0x7F) | 0x80` and shift `u >>= 7`; finally emit the remaining 7-bit chunk `u`.

examples.explanation: n = 0 ZigZag-encodes to u = 0, which fits in one 7-bit byte [0].
n = -100 ZigZag-encodes to u = 199 = 1 * 128 + 71; low 7 bits with continuation flag give 71 | 128 = 199, followed by 1.
